page: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. Provisioned under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with dedicated allocation and simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 768 GB of system memory, matching an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 5670 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The platform does not incorporate dedicated GPU hardware, directing compute resources entirely toward central processing and memory throughput.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the top tier for multi-threaded CPU and memory workloads. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 118,358.18 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 176,827.47. In memory operations, cached 16 KB read bandwidth reaches 9,789.61 GB/sec, while uncached large-block writes sustain 174.6 GB/sec. Data structure benchmarks reflect high throughput, registering 143.37 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 39,136.64.

The dense ratio of memory to compute coupled with 5.67 TB of direct NVMe storage provides strong resource efficiency for stateful and memory-bound operations, eliminating external storage I/O bottlenecks for local cache datasets. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of discrete hardware accelerators, making parallel tensor calculations reliant on AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI extensions. As configured, the server fits large-scale relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, Redis caching layers, and high-volume data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores based on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 768 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPU hardware. Hardware instruction support covers AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic accelerations like AES and SHA-NI. In synthetic testing, the instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress tests, PassMark database benchmarks, and memory write bandwidth, alongside handling over 143 million Redis SET operations per second. The large memory capacity combined with fast local NVMe storage offers balanced density for data-heavy workloads. This configuration is structured for memory-intensive enterprise applications, high-performance in-memory caching, large relational or NoSQL database clusters, and large-scale data engineering workflows.
